title: Throughput drop and embedding quality drift after small-model rollout — kernel-scheduling mismatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A planned rollout of a smaller, faster embedding model variant to reduce token cost triggered an unanticipated throughput regression and intermittent quality drift for the rerank endpoint. The incident manifested as increased tail latency, queueing on the embedding service, and occasional lower BLEU-like ranking agreement on a production prompt set. This ticket captures the operational timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and follow-up actions.

Impact:
- Duration: ~9 hours of degraded performance with sustained elevated 95th/99th percentiles, Jan 18 03:10–12:30 UTC.
- Affected surface: embeddings/rerank hosted endpoints (all regions), ~8% of production traffic routed to the canary model experienced >2x tail latency; ~1.5% of requests showed ranking quality drop vs baseline.
- Customer symptoms: slow responses for batch rerank requests, increased retries from internal downstream service, and one customer-reported SLA alert.

Detection:
- Degraded client-side telemetry alerted on 95th latency via the console alerting rule (rerank:95th > 400ms). Ops paging triggered at 03:20 UTC.
- Automated canary comparisons showed a divergence in latency and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) against the baseline.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2025-01-18 02:40 UTC: Canaries for new small quantized embedding model (v2-small-q4) begin rollout (10% traffic).
- 2025-01-18 03:10 UTC: Alerts fire for increased p95/p99 latency on embeddings service.
- 2025-01-18 03:15 UTC: Oncall escalates and pauses further rollout.
- 2025-01-18 03:25 UTC: Engineering correlates spike with canary traffic; immediate rollback to v2-small-q4->v1-medium.
- 2025-01-18 03:30–05:00 UTC: Partial mitigation — increased autoscale buffer and disabled aggressive batching on the canary pool; latency improved but not fully recovered.
- 2025-01-18 05:05 UTC: Full rollback to baseline model completed; tail latencies return to near-normal by 05:45 UTC.
- 2025-01-18 06:00–12:30 UTC: Post-incident investigation and targeted load tests reproduce the issue.

Root cause analysis:
1) Kernel scheduling mismatch: The smaller quantized model used different attention kernel paths (new fused kernels optimized for smaller sequence length) that triggered suboptimal kernel selection heuristics on a subset of GPU/driver combinations. The runtime scheduler favoured a kernel that performed poorly under mixed concurrent workloads, increasing GPU stall time and creating queuing backpressure.
2) Batch-size distribution shift: Production traffic for rerank requests has a bimodal sequence length distribution. The v2-small-q4 runtime heuristics assumed shorter sequences and selected lower-overhead batching windows; under real traffic with interleaved long and short sequences the scheduling produced backpressure and head-of-line blocking.
3) Insufficient canary isolation: Canary pool shared device profiles with baseline pool (same instance types and kernel cache), leading to cache eviction and cold-start of optimized kernels for baseline workloads when the canary kernel warmed.
4) Minor model quality regression: Quantization introduced small embedding vector distortions for certain token patterns exacerbated by lower effective batch sizes; observed as a small MRR drop on ~1.5% of test prompts.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back the canary and halted rollout (completed by 03:30 UTC).
- Increased autoscale headroom for embedding pools to reduce queuing and added temporary 25% extra capacity.
- Disabled the aggressive micro-batching heuristic for the canary pool to force consistent batching behavior across sequence lengths.
- Opened GPU driver/kernel debug traces and collected kernel selection logs for affected instances.

Reproduction and validation:
- Synthetic traffic generator replayed a production sequence-length mix and reproduced the tail latency increase on affected GPU types (A10G with driver X.Y.Z).
- A/B tests with controlled workloads confirmed MRR regression correlated with the quantized model at 0.8%–1.7% depending on prompt category.

Long-term remediation and follow-ups:
- Runtime change: Improve kernel-selection heuristics to consider mixed sequence-length distributions and concurrent workload profiles (ENG-30890).
- Canary isolation: Ensure canaries run on logically isolated kernel caches / dedicated device pools to avoid cross-pollination (ENG-30912).
- Model-side: Re-run quantization with a more representative calibration set that includes long-query tails and add per-token calibration checks (ENG-30801).
- Autoscale and batching: Add a dynamic batching policy that adapts to observed sequence-length histograms and prioritizes latency SLO for rerank traffic (ENG-31002).
- Testing: Add a synthetic mixed-length stress test to CI that mirrors production interleaving patterns (ENG-30795).
- Observability: Add a canary-quality dashboard that surfaces MRR/precision@k vs baseline and kernel-selection distribution for each device type (ENG-31120).

Decisions taken:
- Hold quantized small model rollout until kernel-selection and canary isolation work complete.
- Prioritize runtime fixes (ENG-30890) as P0 for next runtime sprint.
